The 4 year cycle and why it will continue to work (for the rest of our lives)

For those who have been following my posts for a while, know that I am a big advocate of cycle theory and especially the 4 year cycle, as we have been using it to call the Nov 2021 top and Nov 2022 bottom on $BTC with high confidence recently, and I am determined to call the next cycle top once again on $BTC.

Yes, $BTC is fairly new, but the 4 year cycle has proven to show to work for hundreds of years outside of #bitcoin in stocks, commodities and forex (although forex has been more complex because it introduces two variables of two countries' economies being valued against each other). 

So, I just wanted to quickly point out why the 4 year cycle works so well, why it is 4 years and why it will continue to work probably for the rest of our lives. This is going to be a highly simplified explanation but simple means easy to understand and remember with some common sense so with all that said here we go.

The 4 year cycle works as good as everywhere

To keep things simple, I just took the stock market as an example. Because there are enough 4 year cycle posts on $BTC and so you all already know the four year cycle has worked very well so far due to the assets' high volatility and returns as $BTC is one of the only inventions which have been priced since inception. Also going on about a 4 year cycle with only 4 data points so far is still not that significant statistically thus not ideal. Although I hope to introduce some logic with this post and show that the 4 year cycle goes beyond statistics.

How to identify one cycle

So on the chart below, I've defined each start of the cycle by their lows. This is because the lows define the cycle. Lows are regularly spaced and there is no discretion between an early or late top which are both possible depending on what the economic circumstances are within the 20 year and 100 year cycle, which is the biggest issue if you try to define cycles by their tops. And it's in fact convenient to focus on the lows because that's when you want to be buying and buying at the right time is more important than selling in a market that generally trends up. 

We can see how well the assumption of using lows holds. The average cycle length after indicating cyclical lows is 48.76 over 17 cycles (60+ years of stock market data) and has a very tight standard deviation of below 3 months, which is exceptionally low.

This regular spacing is remarkable and very useful for investors, but also traders (who need the 4 year cycle bias to define the direction of the trend on their swing trades - every market move stems from the high timeframes i.e. 'the high timeframe destinations are the ultimate destinations')

Why is it 4 years and not 5, 6 or 7?

The reason why it is 4 years is up to interpretation and controversial, so to avoid that, I am not discussing it here. But if you understand that money and politics are very tightly connected, and accept as evidence that almost every war or political powerplay is mostly about money, and that the snowball of wealthy countries - strong armies is no coincidence, then I think it's not that hard to imagine.

So assuming that, the eb and flow of a countries wellbeing and capital powerplays are driven by political power shifts, and they are of course shift once every election cycle. And the elections are indeed held every 4 years in the USA, but also other rich entities fall underneath the 4 year mark (UK, Germany, ...). Deviation exists and some elections happen every 3 years and some every 5 years, but on average, it revolves around the number 4. 

There are more arguments on why 4,some are even overarching, but I think this one is the easiest to understand and a good place to start.

20 year and 100 year cycles

What about the 20 year and 100 year cycle? Well, they are multiples of four, so buying lows of 4 year cycles also will give you the lows of the 20 year and 100 year cycles and you will still trade them very well as cycle are intertwined. So to keep things simple and prevent analysis paralysis, you will serve well with the belief in the 4 year cycle and most likely beat 90% using 4 year cycles.

Conclusion

So with that, I've (maybe) convinced you to use 4 year cycles. I'm going to continue to believe in them and continue to design my core investment strategy around that, and continue to use that overall bull or bear market bias to trade in, just like I did in 2022 where I was mainly short and in 2023 and onwards, where I will remain mainly long.

Will you?

TLDR

The markets are cyclical in nature and the most versatile and easiest to understand and apply is arguably the 4 year cycle. It has shown itself to work very well in $BTC, but for much longer in other markets. This cycle is driven by the political power shifts who also shift every 4 year cycles, mainly true in the US, but true on average around the world.

So with that, it makes sense to continue to trust in 4 year cycles, design investment strategies around that and have no excuses to not stay on top of the high timeframe ebbs and flows.

Overall mechanics

So the way this signal works is simple. It is based on the RSI indicator on the weekly timeframe. Now I generally do not like indicators that repaint (moving averages, mac D's, RSI's, where their values sometimes change even after the value is painted on the chart during its candle close), because they can give false signals in real time, while in hindsight they look clean. But the RSI 'close' setting does not repaint.

The main reason though why I like RSI and accept it into my array of data analysis here is because Elliot Wave analysts use it and Ralph Nelson Elliott is one of the all time greats of market analysis and one of the founding fathers of cycle analysis. So RSI is one of the best indicators to support data analysis other than price action when it comes to high timeframe cyclical behavior.

See, in early days (first 30/40 years) of any market (stocks, gold, and $BTC today), the RSI has also clearly (no false signals) indicated when a market 'fully resets' and when it transfers into peak momentum 'pre blowoff top' until it reaches a top and momentum fully transferred over into price (the final and most aggressive stage of the bull run).

Now I don't like using RSI to buy bottoms because there are far easier and more straightforward signals (although it is a nice confluence). But I do like to use it to see in what stage of the momentum the market is. And when you hear "momentum", I don't mean in a discretionary way as you see most of the time, but in a simple, clear cut, to the point and easy to identify way without any possible confusion or bias fitting.

Application to $BTC

Indeed, each time RSI reaches above 85, the market enters the "peak momentum stage". Once the market is in peak momentum, it continues up, making new cycle highs into the final run. I.e. it continues up rather than down. 

As you know, there are traps and consolidations inside of the final run, of course (otherwise everyone would make money and it would be too easy). But by the playbook of modern cycle theory's RSI usage, peak momentum will never reach under the midpoint (RSI = 42.5). Most traders use 50 RSI level to be less conservative and only catch the most aggressive of trades on lower timeframes, so if you see that, this is where it comes from.

And as we can see, after reaching 85 for the first time in each cycle (after the reset of 35), indeed the 42.5 level never gets crossed and has no fake signals.

Finally, once the peak occurred and we had massive mania, that is when the market needs a full shift in momentum to build it back up, which happens at RSI = 35. In most assets, this is 30, but because $BTC is still in its early stages, 35 suffices for a reset.

And while I do believe the impact of interest rates on the price of $BTC (or stocks) is important, it is not as straightforward as portrayed and is often just misconstrued and a more careful conclusion is required. There are people who devote their lives to calling the types of effects they have and spend extensive hours trying to pinpoint a stock market crash (like Michael Bury). And although people like that are often mocked, they are in fact geniuses (if they make money from it) and even they are indeed wrong now and then because it is in fact extremely difficult to call such scenarios exact using that approach, which is why we rather stick to different methods. 

So with that, I do believe you will have a more informed view after reading this, and my stronger claims/hope is that you will never be impacted by said oversimplified 'macro' analysis ever again, and instead, will have a more critical stance towards any 'data' shown to you, even if it's as important as 'the impact of interest rates'.

Oversimplified and out-of-context macro analysis

So I've openly called the #bitcoin bottom beginning of August. And given the current situation with interest rates, there is a lot of doubt in my call and I very often get asked why I don't fear interest rates being high (or low), neither all the macro analysts opposing my stance at the moment. Because after all, #BTC (and stocks) still are risk-on asset, thus heavily impacted by interest rates.

The problem is that said macro analysis is done in a simple way. People look at 'what interest rates have done in history'. So doing such analysis, you would divide the chart up in periods of what the interest rates have done in the past and what the stock market did and make a conclusion on today. In the example below, I chose the stock market, similar analysis applies to $BTC, but there is less data available.

Now the fear of today comes from the fact that the FED is about to pivot into decreasing interest rates again. Makes sense and I have nothing against that, I believe it will happen too as that's just the normal cycle of inevitabilities. But the permabears and impressionists often use this argument to say that "dropping interest rates cause risk-on market drops". A strong stance to take which, sure, with a contrarian market view could make sense, as 'in 2000 and 2008, it happened'. But here's the issue we already highlighted in a previous rant: this is using 2 data points to predict the future and at the same time, used completely out of context. Sure it's just statistics, but they are in fact using statistics in this case (whether they are aware of it or not) to predict what should happen today.

So here just my word to kindly take a grain of salt when you see the market analyzed this way (or you catch yourself doing it this way, as ever so often, I do myself).

Instead: a more in depth look

You don't have to believe me, just look at the data. Based on history, we can clearly see that the market also went up plenty of times during interest rate drops (see chart: Interest rates Down, Market Up or I D M U). And the amount of times that happened was equal to the amount of times we had the market dropping during interest rate drops (Interest rates Down, Market Down or I D M D). So even in recent history, it is a toss up.

We also see that when interest rates go up, the market went up (I U M U). Indeed on the chart below, that is true. But in 1972 for instance, interest rates went up and market went down (I U M D). You could even argue that the recent 30% decline in 2022 was a similar situation. And in 1974, the market went up upon dropping interest rates (I D M U). So if anything, you could say the market right now should continue up with dropping interest rates rather than down. But I also don't stand by that because that's also trying to fit a bias using only one data point. So no matter what happened, we clearly see there is no meaningful correlation with what happened to interest rates versus what happened with the market.

So all this data, is just data. There is nothing meaningful behind it. That's okay, but it's a skill (mostly common sense) to recognize when data has no meaningful impact, which we indeed also concluded here. 

Where these pitfalls stem from

The reason analysis like this is so popular is because this type of approach offers proof for both the bullish and bearish stance, which is why analysts love to use it as there always is a case to fit their bias, or for the 'unbiased' analyst to say 'just watch the interest rates and react' (which is mostly too late) or speculate on a case and create content/for your entertainment, as, something as big as interest rates is easy to get an impression on.

Conclusion (personal opinion)

So with that, I've made my point. When data shows no one sided view and is not useable, it's something what we call 'noise' in the field of system theory, and so it's in my opinion smart to both recognize and treat it that way. 

One (the only) way this type of approach can be useful is perhaps if you are an absolute genius who has a highest level in depth understanding of what markets do in the current conditions using convoluted logic (people like Michael Bury). But I believe using history and forming a simple comparison is not sufficient and fits into the category of strong confirmation bias analysis. The same is very often true with random out-of-context fractals.

Alternatively, you could just believe that there is an agnostic that both controls the interest rates/the macro money flow and the market prices at the same time, as we do... 

So here's my stance on the most common data analysis you see out there involving interest rates, and that it is mostly just noise IMO, as I've been trying to prove here.

As always, feel free to disagree.

To finish up the data analysis considering whether this is a good time to buy, I included one more set of data analysis with once again powerful results (16 data points over the entire history of #bitcoin's existence) once more. The mechanics of the hash ribbons are fairly simple: each time a cross up happens, the buy signal flashes. This comes from an increase of the hash rate after a steep drop i.e. a compromise of the networks hash rate, a direct consequence of miners capitulation. However, this is not just a simple 'buy signal flash'. It is the first best signal that flashes after true miners capitulation i.e. a signal carrying fundamental logic. 

See each time the price drops significantly, miners become compromised due to their profits decreasing because their returns drop (see the quoted post). If the price drops even further, ultimately some miners have to shut down their business (and liquidate their bitcoin). This is true miner capitulation. This shutdown of miner businesses is quantifiable as it drops down the entire #BTC network hash rate and thus gives a cross down on the hash ribbons. The candle closed higher

I asked you if the final candle on the chart would close lower or higher, and it indeed closed higher.

Despite the chart "looking bad" locally, the candle managed to gain support and bounced within that same candle.

Many had it wrong, some had it right, but you all tried.

The reason the candle closed higher is simple. It is because the candle took previous candles' high, which means it very likely will not take previous candles' low in the same candle. This is the framework of the famous OHLC theory.

It may seem not that useful but you would be surprised how many times the market shows itself that way, because it is a great way to trap the unaware player. It also often forms that perfect time to countertrade many overhyped people expecting continuation during the exact wrong times.

It works on every timeframe, in every direction, on every asset.

Don't believe me? I invite you to back test it yourself, you will see that only a tiny fraction of historic candles have taken both the previous' candle high and previous candle low (where this gets invalidated). And even if it does, it generally retests the previous candle low/high, so you have a chance to get out break even.

So every time you see a candle move above the high and then move close to previous candle low, that's a great confluence for a potential long with a stoploss below previous' candle low, or, a great time to close shorts, or to not enter shorts as you just sparked your awareness once again through reading this.

Best of all, this requires no context. Or, this theory is the high time frame context in these specific cases (where, the examined candle subjected to an OHLC is your high timeframe and the trade shaped in the low timeframe, inside the candle).

Information I haven't seen talked about (nowhere close to enough) on crypto or trading twitter.

While our $BTC long trade idea is going fully to plan, just going to post another slight(ly) (controversial) rant here, because well, trading and investing successfully involves accepting the right controverse, which is why only a small percentage comes out on top (those who see through all the non-sense).

Also had a lot of success and eye-opening discussion on here on our last rant, which is nice to see because you all seem to have an open mind towards these type of things. And I do believe it will open the eyes of many once again so here you go.

Everything below, just my opinion for your entertainment on my philosophy on how to trade and invest (fearlessly) and how to not worry about the news or black swans at any point in time. Also some real life examples included on #bitcoin / #crypto because that's what I almost exclusively trade and invest in. 

Going to keep it short and sweet, not lifting the full thesis but just sparking your interest and critical minds, because going deep will need a longer form post and longer reading so trying to prevent that. That aside, here we go.

Black swans and news events defined

So before starting, just my quick thoughts on what a Black Swan (BS) and general news events are. Essentially they are both the same, and BS's are of the worst end (news events could be positive). So I am just going to talk about black swans and you can assume news falls under the same umbrella, where black swans are negative, apply the opposite to positive events. 

So aside from the definition of "a BS is something very bad that happened and causes markets to drop", I am giving it a slightly different definition of "a BS is a single moment in time, in which an excuse is framed for the market to drop sharply towards current demand". 

See it's never longer than pretty much a single day or sometimes week and it's never deeper than where heavy demand is locally. It is also never "the end of everything" or "an event that could nuke $BTC back to sub 10k". And while I'm not saying that couldn't happen ever, I am saying that it can't happen if a black swan where to happen right now.

Just think about it, why did the covid black swan take us down to 4000$, but why did the event of escalations involving Israel not take us anywhere close? Seemingly, that news is way worse, right? And why did the day of Russia invading Ukraine not make us drop more than 10% whilst it was arguably one of the worst events of the first half of this decade in terms of political distress. Why did price go lower afterwards, through events totally unrelated to war, rather just through the natural market cycle of leveraging - deleveraging. And why did the FTX collapse not take us down more than 30%, whilst FTX was probably one of the biggest market movers at the time?

I am sure you all have a reason for yourself. But it's truly important to question these things and try to have a holistic view. There is no absolute in the consequences on the market price of black swans. They don't always  give a bad drop (if ever out of bounds) and they don't always form the bottom. 

And once you assume that philosophy, you understand that there is no need to be afraid for black swans, you can invest without the fear of them happening. And even better, if they happen, knowing this will stop you from panic selling or buy more with a calm mind, and thus allow you to be a holistic and successful investor, seeing them as an opportunity.

Forget black swans, learn cycle theory

So, I just told you that black swans (and news drivers) don't have a large impact if at all on the high timeframes and in fact shouldn't be feared, if ever especially if you are an investor. 

So why do black swans not always create a bottom and why are there such inconsistencies on their result?

This is where the definition comes in. They are IMO an excuse for the market to drop towards "whale demand" and for price to be manipulated to that area. In other words, during a black swan, price does nothing but move towards where whales want the market to move to, (mostly the current high timeframe demand). And the high timeframe demand levels eb and flow and change over time, along with the cyclical nature of the markets. This is why the Ukraine invasion didn't take us down to 4k and covid did. This is also why you shouldn't hope or wait for any black swan in the future in the hopes to buy at 4k if the current cyclical demand is way higher. This is also why you shouldn't get shaken out of your $BTC spot positions you bought near the bottom if said "black swan" happened near the top (not too long ago). And most importantly, this is also why you shouldn't fear black swans triggering a bear market. I mean look at the covid crash, it trigger a bull market, i.e. the opposite.

And yes, a valid excuse: that last one was because of the money printer. Sure. Well if you believe in the cyclical money printer, you must believe in the leverage-deleveraging cycles because they go hand in hand.

Conclusion: its all about the market cycles

So now with all that said, it just comes down to one conclusion: trust market cycles, and do not worry about the news, (trust the opposite of the news).

To understand that, it is beneficial to understand how market cycles work. Not without going too in depth here. But cycles are nothing but equally spaced time intervals where the overall paradigm continuously shifts back and forth from "prices are low" to "prices are high" back to "prices are low", rinse and repeat.. Along with that, evolves whales their willingness to bid and sell higher and "whales their willingness to bid only lower and sell also less high". 

See the chart below on both boundaries marked in Blue (whale demand) and Red (whale supply). If a black swan happens, it only takes price (closer) to whale demand, if good news happens, price moves to whale supply. This explains why black swans do not take price excessively low (or good news excessively high). It explains why the covid crash didn't take price below 3k, because we were already progressed further in the (monetary) cycle, this is also why the Ukraine invasion nuked us to sub 12k (what many were calling for) and why price went lower after (because the cycle allowed us to do so). And finally, this also explains why the current black swan didn't take us much further down than 50k. Instead, if you truly want price to move further, that takes time. And that is true for many reasons I won't go in right now, but just think of big money. That takes time to move.

It's a beautiful conclusion (if you accept it). Because waiting for prices takes time instead (it's not going to happen on one BS event), time to wait for the cycle to progress to it favoring your prices (whether for buying or selling) is the essence of successful investing (and trading on the lower timeframes, because trading = investing on the lower timeframes and vice versa). This philosophy also alleviates stress, because nothing unpredictable can get in the way of your investments/trades.

And with that said, you understood once again, that time is the most important element of the market. Only those who can wait, can win.

$BTC data analysis

Regarding seasonality - 82% chance on a bullish Q4

September is about to close and to the general public's surprise, it's looking like it's going to be green (by a long shot), with the chance of setting the greenest September in 2024, supporting our breakout thesis we have been on for a while now. 

And although we're not the only ones anymore that are on the full bull thesis, data is and remains data. And after thorough inspection, despite the talking/analysis posts, most are not positioned yet, took profit too early or will cheer for dips and say they are a gift for the reason of wanting one.

This observation is not just coming from public posts or twitter, but also from the array of paid groups partaken in to conduct these analyses. Not allowed to share names or details, but most groups indeed are long and took profit early, are looking for an entry, or are short. So the market's hand seems to be working. 

The data

So indeed, this analysis is about seasonality and month-to-month performance. And although I do not classify this as my primary consideration of what to expect from the market as it carries a high variability, seasonality has a lot to do with the cyclical nature of markets and portrays the strong momentum $BTC typically has.

The data analysis is fairly simple here: each time $BTC had a green September, it was followed by no less than three green months after, i.e. a green October, November and December. And this happened 3/3 times since $BTC inception. So technically, there is a 100% chance this happens again. 

Own criticism

Now like I said, I am not the biggest fan of seasonality and our analysis only has 3 data points, which gives us only a 67% confidence to make the claim that the next three months will indeed be green (low data fallacy). But to add significance, by the binary nature of bullish/bearish, there is also exclusivity to the data: if September is not green, 6 out of 8 times, Q4 has not been green each month. So, by including the exclusivity, a more general and easier to interpret claim, using more datapoints is that:

"The direction of September has determined the general direction of Q4 and if September is green and not red, a bullish (not bearish) Q4 has followed 9 out of 11 times. So if September closes above 59k, there is an 82% chance Q4 will be bullish".

How bullish? We will see (time is more important than price), but it's not about planning for retirement and making fast money. It's about being on the right side of the trade, time after time after time, enjoying the market stress free and not having too many regrets  through losing money or being sidelined (enjoying the process). And this way, eventually (rather soon), you hit your goals.

I personally think it's going to be quite a good run though, one not to be underestimated.

TLDR

Green September suggest an 82% chance of a good and easy mode Q4. This is based on data valid since $BTC's inception. Not only data, but also confirmed by how the bulk of the crypto trader communities are positioned after critical inspection, showing the hand of the market is working.

They created $DOGE in 2013 as a joke to have a cryptocurrency that shouldn't be taken as seriously as $BTC, for retail to trade (which $BTC taken very seriously at the time). They liked the idea of inflation because every fiat currency has that and it is in fact healthy for the economy to have some (not too much) inflation.

The coin is indeed created in 2013 which makes it one of the first altcoins ever created. Many altcoins come and go every cycle but this fact alone together with their high profile team makes #dogecoin unforgettable in my opinion. But not just in my opinion, also in opinion of the entire world.

But we know there have been bull and bear markets in between which are hard to call 'a range'. So, before continuing, I first need to give a definition of how I defined a range in this analysis, where it begins, and where it ends, because there is a lot of discretion there.

Definition of a macro range

A range is a period of time of price moving up and down between two price points. Now, I personally limited those two price points to not be more than double from each other. So the move from range high to range low is no larger than a 50% drop. This is an arbitrary choice, but I think you can all agree that the drop from the top in May 2021 to the bottom in June 2021 should not be considered a range anymore, nor the rally from the low in June 2021 to the high in November 2021 either. Respective high-low differences are a -55% and -58% drop. So that is where I draw the line.

And I also think we can all agree that the drop from the June 2019 highs to the covid crash lows are also not part of the same range, but instead an entire bear market on its own.

All other price boundaries are indeed ranges.

Next, I need to define when the range begins and ends. And with the number one theorem to define ranges: the midrange theorem, that is quite easy:

'a range begins and ends when it visits the midrange point for the first and the last time'. That's IMO very intuitive as, when you expect the price no longer to return to the midpoint, it also won't continue to range lows (if a breakout is coming) or range highs (if a breakdown is coming). So that definition also allows you to position at the midrange (the classic midrange consolidation) before breaking out or breaking down. In other words, this definition not only defines the range cleanly, it also is great for execution.

And the cherry on the cake, this definition also automatically causes at least a 50% drop or 100% pump after a breakout by the nature of my definition. (otherwise, I would still count it under the same range).

The reason I tie 'recession' and 'yield inversion' together is because according to macro 'analysts' of today, yield inversion is the cause of a recession (and bear market) and it's a trend that has caught on. If you don't believe me, just google the words 'yield inversion', and you will see 'recession' follow up. So the association of both together is highly popular.

And although that may be true to some extent and in some contexts, I personally think it's more complex than that, so complex in fact that it is not a direct cause at all, rather just a mere correlation. A bad one, in fact, with a lot of noise and false signals. I also think that the charts more important than the YIN (yield inversion narrative), and I'm also here to just show you that that narrative is indeed noise rather than data with a proper skew if we look at historic values properly. 

I say properly here because most analysts compare it only to 2000 and 2008, make their post/blog/YT video/launch their website, bank their ad revenue and call it a day, or, perhaps more mildly speaking, they have lived through 2000 and 2008 and have been hurt by it or close relatives have been. So they are subjected to the recency bias and short term memory fallacy which is a fair point of fear. But I am here to provide proper in depth and unbiased analysis to give you a more critical view and show you that that data is just noise and nothing else. So without any further introduction, let's begin.

What is yield inversion?

So first, a quick definition what 'Yield Inversion' means because it's funnily enough not known everywhere even throughout my own crypto and equity circles of consistent traders.

So the US Gov releases bonds. These bonds are a contract where you lend money to the US gov and receive yield from them in a form of interest in return. Since these bonds are leased by the US Gov, they are considered safe, which is why bonds are considered one of the safest forms of investment (only the collapse of the government would mean a compromise of those investments).

Now, the longer you lend your money to the US Gov, the higher the interest rate should be because, well you are locking up your money for longer thus that is a higher commitment and a higher risk which should come with higher rewards and which is generally the case.

These interests change constantly over time and in fact are determined by the market. These markets are indeed the 2Y, 5Y, 10Y, 30Y etc. ticker available on TradingView.

Now, yes these rates change but they change quite slowly, and need to be (at least partially) coherent with whatever the interest rates are, which is also the reason why the 10Y and the Fed interest rates are moving in lockstep together with a slight shift in time.

And as I mentioned, the higher the time horizon, the higher the yield should be. And the times where this is not the case is called 'yield inversion'.

Why a recession is feared upon yield inversion

So, in the light of 'recession fear', yield inversion refers to 2Y being higher than the 10Y. 

But there are far yield inversions possible, such as the 2Y reaching above the 5Y, or the 5Y above the 10Y or even the 10Y above the 30Y, in fact, every single point in time where the relative values of two arbitrary yields do not 'make sense' is when we speak of yield inversion. These inversions are abnormal, and because both the 2000 and 2008 collapse both had a 2Y-10Y yield inversion, macro analysts associate this with the fear of a recession. 

So on the chart below I've marked out these times, and all the other times throughout history when the 2Y-10Y yield curve has been inverted on the S&P500.

And here is the first problem in my opinion. Because both the 2000 and 2008 collapse both had the 2Y-10Y yield inversion, macro 'analysts' cherry picked this inversion to support their bias.

And for those who have been following my posts for a while know that any analysis only involving two data points are rather meaningless, especially if there is no logic involved and especially if there are also false signals involved (which large nullifies any possible direct logic).

Indeed, we can see prior to the 2000 and 2008 collapse, the yield curve was inverted, but in the 1980's, the market just kept moving along peacefully. So that's only an accuracy of 66% ánd using only 3 data points. And saying 'it happened in 2000 and in 2008 so it will happen right now' is no sound logic, only statistics, with a very low amount of data points.

As you know, my standards are far higher, and I think this debunks the fear of recession due to 2Y-10Y yield inversion' by quite a long shot. In fact, we are seeing quite the opposite and the markets are thriving. You can say that 'a recession is coming in the future', sure. But those callers clearly missed the bottom and are clearly exposed to upside and sidelined risk so some re-assessment is required (unless their business thrives on stirring fear, then good for them, but I'm not buying it).

Is yield inversion meaningless?

Now with all that said, I'm going to introduce my own logic and understanding and how to interpret this data as, based on what I presented, does this really mean that yield inversion means absolutely nothing? 

Of course not. It's still an anomaly. And that's still a good thing to know. It means there is something abnormal going on with the economy. But to link 'something unusual' with the 'market will crash soon', is once again far beyond our capacity and only geniuses like Michael Bury have been able to make money off of this, occasionally. But even he did that through deep research that goes far beyond just a simple inversion. In fact, he was smart enough to recognize he had to devote all his time to go deep into the housing bubble, which was the direct cause of the economy to collapse, not the yield inversion.

In the second chart, I provided all the yield inversions of all yields that happened throughout history. And you can see how there is barely any correlation worth paying attention, which really should make you question: is the current yield inversion really indicative of price?

So with this, I hope I not only explained, but also showed with significant and unbiased proof that indeed, calling market crashes based on this type of data is merely useful and rather a tactic to stir up recession fear for news channels to get views, or for macro 'analysts' a basis to fall back on so they can be able to tell you 'I told you so', in case a market crash happens.

You won't see me do that here, you know my analysis is different as we believe the truth is in the charts instead and in significant data and/or sound logic they portray.

And with that, I hope you'll have more confidence in your investments, do not buy (or rather do not panic sell) fear that is presented as I just described or at least read these types of posts with a more critical view for the rest of your life. And instead you'll be more inclined to make decisions based off significant data and/or logic with more confidence, even if it's during 'recession fear', just like when we called for and bought the #BTC bottom during the entire 15-25k range.

The 90.88% macro bullish breakout chance now increased to 95.23%

So, two weeks ago we posted an extensive in-depth analysis of why we think $BTC will break out and not break down from this range.

It was received quite well since the entire analysis was fully unbiased, with a conclusion drawn from a total of 4 data analyses each having very strong data suggesting eventual upside. At the same time, we also made in-depth post after in-depth post, trying to find things that counter our argument. Yet none of them had any significance, debunking some very common crypto-macro financial myths at the same time.

The analyses consist of bottom signals and breakout signals. The price at the time of posting the bottom signals was 56k and the price at the time of posting the breakout signals was around the current price.

All of the analyses have no false signals, and consist of at least 15 data points, valid without any selectivity, over at least 7 years of data. Quite unusual to the typical analysis made on the platform as those either are heavily bias or hindsight fitted or carry generally no more than just one or two cases compared to today, mostly also only cherry picking bear cases out of fear, such as 'in 2008 this happened so now it will happen again' or something along those lines. It may be correct, but as you know, my standards are higher in terms of statistical data, therefore, I tried to be patient to find signs that carry more than 15 cases each and every time.

The update

And one of them, was by measuring length of consolidations.

In the quoted post, we created a logical, non-discretionary and fully systematic definition of how to identify macro consolidations. And based on that definition, there was a 90% chance we would break away in the next 4 weeks at the time. Now, we are two weeks further, and price tapped the midline (60.2k) quite accurately once again. According to the definition, this means that the length has been extended once again, now to a whopping 31 weeks.

At the same time, I decided to make the definition less forgiving, and include tighter consolidations and change the older data, as the first data set still included consolidations that could be argued to be inclusive of too big of moves (90%+ moves). So I changed the definition to 50%.

In other words, once a range is broken, the next range high will be at least 50% higher than the previous range high. $BTC.D Update

Will we never have a proper altcoin season again?

Alts are still at low prices and $BTC.D is raging up and yes, $ETH (and altcoin) holders are having a tough time.

With the recent Uptober disbullief, altcoins dropping heavily and $BTC maxis celebrating their $BTC heavy allocation, I think there is a lot of disbelief now that $BTC.D can go back down and doubt if we will have an altcoin season at all. So no better time than to check the facts about what most likely is going to happen.

You hear things like '$BTC ETF changed everything'
'Boomers will not buy altcoins which is why they won't go up'. '$BTC is at ATH and alts have done nothing'. Which are all things that are easy to say and grasp because they fit the current chart perfectly so they give you a sense of comfort and a reason to not hold any alts (which is typically rough during accumulation stages, especially if the $BTC chart 'looks' a lot better).

But we know better and you know how I don't follow narratives (and rather counter them) by looking at data, proof and market logic (which is different than conventional logic from the media), which is how we were able to make moves like buying the $BTC cycle bottom sub 22k, calling the move from 30k to 70k etc, whilst the majority was believing the counternarrative. Not only that, we also are acting on it as we recently started buying altcoins again for the second time this entire 4 year cycle, where the first time was around the cycle bottom.

The 'altcoin season is dead' narrative IMO is one of the easiest narratives to counter and I'll lay out the facts here as unbiased as possible of what will happen to our altcoins. Before that however, I am giving a quick definition of what I understand under altcoin season. 

Own definition

A true altcoin season is one where liquidity from the most dominant asset ($BTC) flows to the other assets ($ETH and altcoins). As a consequence, $BTC.D drops and nearly all altcoins go up. Note how this definition does not say anything about your altcoins going up necessarily. You could have picked the early runners that already performed really well in part one of the cycle ($FET, $ONDO, $RNDR, $WIF to give some arbitrary examples). So 'some altcoins going up a lot' is not altcoin season to my definition. Those early runners are a minority and heavily narrative driven and don't require $BTC's liquidity (they don't require a dropping $BTC.D) to run so their run is not part of the big altcoin season. 

That's why I define altcoin season as a $BTC liquidity driven one, where the majority of the altcoins run, which is why the $BTC.D chart is so important.

With that said, now on to the facts of why said altcoin season is still coming.

The facts

1⃣First fact: we had the big altcoin season every single cycle (4 year rotation) like clockwork. That's in the charts but also in our memories if you were active at the time. So you would have to believe in the 'this time is different' scenario if you don't believe it will happen this time which is by default putting yourself in a preliminary disadvantage (because history rhymes/repeats).

2⃣ The $BTC.D chart is on track with its 4 year cycle. As we posted a few months ago, we said that a top is close and likely to come around month 34 to 38. We are now month 33 in the 4 year cycle, which means the tides are about to shift in just a few months. Thinking it will keep going up is essentially thinking that 4 year cycles no longer work. But who knows, maybe you are a genius, maybe you know something both Ralph Nelson Elliott and William Delbert Gann never knew, all power to you.

3⃣ The 'first Grand Altcoin rotation' generally happens once per cycle: around Q4 in year 3 of the cycle and is again playing out like clockwork so far. 

For the ones who weren't around, 2018-2022 had a clear grand altcoin rotation which could be felt by both parties (who acted correctly and who didn't act correctly on it). This means that some altcoins (a minority) run strongly early in the cycle whilst other get left behind, where most of the others put in their big gains late in the cycle whilst the ones that ran early receive lackluster gains in the second half because they are already overbought and whales are looking to exit (they just care about the money). 

There is a whole book you could write about why this is, but it has in essence to do with alt coin rotations also being subjected to cycle theory (as everything is). We have seen very clear proof of that in 2018-2022 already (the first real cycle where a lot of altcoins exist). In this cycle, in the first 3 years, $LINK is a great example as it was one of the strongest top 100 altcoins for example and has put in a 100x, while $ETH (and all the other $BTC liquidity driven altcoins) have put in a measly 3x. Where during the last year, $ETH has put in a 10x, and $LINK has only gained another 3x or so. 

This proves that in 2019, $LINK was an early altcoin runner, while coins like $ETH need $BTC's liquidity and therefore is a countertrend $BTC.D driven runner. We are seeing the same now, where some altcoins have put in all time high after all time high, and others haven't even come out of their bear market yet. So if the same exact altcoin rotation is happening again right as we speak, why would that rotation suddenly be canceled and why would altcoin season not happen?

4⃣ The $BTC ETF narrative to cancel alt season is way overrated. Yes, the #BTC ETF is great in the long run because it gives #bitcoin an excellent form of TradFi acceptance. But if we simply look at the traded volume, ETF total flows ever since launch have only been accumulated up to 40 billion $. While $BTC CEX volumes are averaging 20 billion every single day. I think it's easy to claim that ETF flows are negligible which is why you never heard me talk about them as I like to filter noise.

5⃣ Favorable monetary policy is around the corner. Interest rates are on the decline, the US money supply is increasing drastically (where now also China is following suit). The only thing we are waiting for is QE, which is typically a natural consequence of M2 increasing (with a delay). The monetary policy shifting in our favor typically also means altcoins do well.

6⃣ $BTC being at ATH is an arbitrary gage to when alt season begins and the fact that it reached ATH but altcoin season hasn't begun yet is IMO not valid to call it canceled. Not the most important claim, but it is often thrown around which is why I like to debunk it. In reality, time (cycles) is the most important factor.

TLDR

So, despite the narrative of altcoins being dead, there is very strong evidence that altcoin season will happen again just like other times, at around the same exact time. The most common narratives given are debunked and the altcoin monetary flow is likely to shift from early, non $BTC liquidity driven runners (minority) to late, $BTC liquidity driven runners, which is in alignment with the $BTC.D chart,  the shifting monetary policy and the typical 4 year behavior that is rhyming once again this time so far.

Yes, it sounds all nice and great, but catching it correctly is another story. It's challenging to catch and buy the bottom on something as volatile as an altcoin because you could face 30% or even 50% drops yet still be close to buying the bottom before a 1,000% run. That's why most won't successfully do it even if they are aware of the above. But with the right timing, a hybrid lump sum and post lump-sum DCA strategy is effective if you can time the market. Which I do think we will be able to do with our recent posts where we started buying again in the last few weeks. We will see. But I think it's going to look great in the future once it all happened.

I could always be wrong. But I enjoy this type of speculation especially if many market-logical things line up and no one really believes in it and/or knows how to act on it.

$BTC and $ETH macro outlook

Beautiful developments

Another month and a half has passed, and the full macro breakout thesis is really pushing many eyes onto the crypto charts now.

Last time we posted our plan of a Q4 upside breakout, $BTC was at 58k and $ETH was at 2.3k. We had our thesis in place, with multiple data analyses supporting not only that the low is in, but also that we likely would see a high timeframe breakout, which is why we have stopped trading the range for the first time ever since calling the local top in March '24. 

Now it's six months later and with all the data supporting us, a move up in Q4 is and remains very likely. Data analysis indeed because our typical order flow and price action analysis, which remains very strong for the low timeframes, simply doesn't work as well on the high timeframe positions and bias. Which is why I seek edge elsewhere. We've established that and.. with $BTC up a strong 20% and $ETH up 13%, against all the low timeframe technical analysis users' belief, before the full breakout even happened, it showed and it's paying of well so far.

Full breakout hasn't happened yet indeed, but that definition is discretionary, which is why we always put in the time and effort to position before the breakout (or breakdown in bear markets). Consequentially, our positions are well comfortable now and what appears to be counter sentiment is now turning into consensus sentiment that a breakout becomes inevitable whilst both $BTC and $ETH ( $ETH slower than $BTC ) are grinding up slowly.

$BTC macro

To find weekly cycle lows, I use time and verify it with sentiment and volume, and the Middle East capitulation event clearly formed that, timed well 28 weeks after the previous weekly cycle low. No hindsight, we called that, drew out a path we most likely saw develop, and since, the sideways price action has indeed shifted more to upside price action. Next weekly low is not due until most likely late December, so there is still room for upside. 

I do indeed expect price to accelerate here. Seems consensus by now, the market always finds a way to escape on the low timeframes as most traders ('investors') find themselves trapped into short term memory fallacy and simply forget the high timeframe picture. Overall peak still expected in the second half of 2025, where I think the true time to 'sell it all' may occur.

$ETH macro

Same outlook as $BTC, but as we discussed, the intertwinement of their cycles is compressed. Meaning, $BTC goes up and down more smoothly, where $ETH typically drops later near the 4 year cycle peaks (2014, 2018,2022)  and has its surge also later in the 4 year cycle (2016, 2020,...) making its moves seem more aggressive. We've drawn this out as well and that's also developing quite well.

Sentiment wise, it also lines up. It's clear by now that 'useful' coins are deemed 'useless', typical things called for when price doesn't move. Yet anyone who even remotely used $ETH knows what it can do. 

Quite ironic to call layer 1's useless as almost all the meme coins ever are created on layer 1's such as $ETH and $SOL.

So, I think the reason utility is not going up yet is purely a cyclical and sentimental matter. We've seen massive hype around it in 2021 and that simply hasn't been digested yet. Hence why they don't go up and hence why bored traders create memes and gamble away there as volatility currently can be found there.

What to prepare for in case I'm wrong

Despite all the data, there still always is a small chance I'm wrong. I've been wrong once on the macro where I thought pre FTX collapse was the bottom around 17k, not after. But indeed at the time, holding positions was the right thing to do, hence why macro and spot positions are so powerful.

If a similar event were to occur, call it WW3, call it the end of a nation or something unexpected, it can always pull down the market significantly, and that would also be a drop, back below 50k. 

Cycles are powerful in nature, and we've shown why those events shouldn't faze you. I will indeed hold on in that case, hedged with large shorts well timed and just continue to ride out the cycle as I do think price will recover from there.

Conclusion

So, as ironic as it sounds, both $BTC and $ETH are playing out pretty close to exactly the way we had hoped for. We've been calling very early on a ranging market and also when it would break out. And now we're here and have been developing full conviction on that it indeed would happen. We're seeing clear signs, I think the bias remains up, and we'll continue to focus.

Not a perma-bullish mindset, we've been 'perma-bearish' the entirety of 2022, 'perma-bullish' the entirety of 2023 and range trading the entirety of 2024. I'll still take low timeframe shorts every now and then, even during up moves, but selectivity just needs to be higher or else you'll just end up in bad positions, lots of stop losses, or even loss of confidence in your edge as the downside targets that get hit in range trading simply don't reach anymore and you'll start to question why.

We'll see how it develops. But so far, so good.

$BTC and #crypto

The importance to treat low timeframes and high timeframes differently in crypto.

Quoting a post here that at the time was taken with a lot of criticism.

Didn't care too much. As it's been a lot of fun seeing this one develop 'against all odds', the OI traders, the 'range traders', the 'resistance' shorts, you name it.

Yes the odds were 'against' us. But where they real odds?

If you have been following me for a while, you've probably already picked up on which data I trust and which I don't and why I value other data than usual for high timeframe moves.

For low timeframe, yes, your order flows, your footprint charts, your OI, your TPO's, your price action, your order books, they work extremely well (if used correctly), and that's why I use them myself. 

And yes, 'price is fractal' (low timeframe price action analysis also works on high timeframes). But that's not true for the other metrics I just mentioned. At the same time, crypto is unique in the sense that it has the highest 1/liquidity*( whale wallets / small wallets) numbers. So timing a macro breakout (and consequentially time big moves), takes a different type of analysis and logic and that's exactly why and when range traders (LTF traders) get caught off guard when high timeframe takes over, despite the fact that having a gage on high timeframes at all times is important.

If you have been surprised or felt a difference in how the market was acting and couldn't understand why your typical analysis may not have worked, that may have been why.

It didn't. As you can see, in October 2020 and October 2023, it also spiked to new highs and made a large rally, many were shorting into it and took a big toll.

So yes, in range trading (LTF trading), OI peaking (if it's fueled by longs, big if) is bearish.

But on a large scale, it simply moves with prices.

This creates a lot of confusion and is why HTF and LTF is important to make a distinction of.

Here is the interpretation:

On large timeframes, it shows how OI typically moves with price.

Higher prices, higher OI, lower prices lower OI.

However, large spikes on low timeframes often lead to local washouts. Depending on whether OI consists of long or shorts, that means, OI has power and logic on low timeframes, but just an observation on high timeframes.

Just my own opinion (NFA).

And that requires timing (early), the right project, the team making no mistakes on the project itself ('getting the meme factor right') and a little bit of luck. I've turned a blind eye to some I should've bought but I didn't to my regret. Examples are $MANEKI, $NEIRO, $POPCAT and $FLOKI back in the days all found relatively early. Can't catch them all and we did catch $PEPE, $BOBO, $CHAD, $TRUE and $TREMP all not too long after launch and they performed exceptionally well (over 20x), but of course I wish to have caught one in 2024, did not happen yet and I just sat there in their telegram not acting on it.

But finally, after learning from mistakes of not acting, or just waiting out until I'm confident enough to buy, $SCOOT came in out the right time, as a quality project launched at the right time (perhaps not coincidental).
 
Fundamentals

1⃣So, first point is that the meme coin I wanted to buy had to be a dog coin. Yes we had Cat Coin season, SOL Meme season, Pepe Offspring season, Presidential Candidate season, but the Dog Coin seems to be the type of coin that keeps on returning. Also looking at instagram pages, social media trends, and overall hype, the most popular animal is and always will be the dog, translating to crypto. And, indeed dog coin season keeps is just always present as the standard, where the rest just comes and goes. 'The dog days will never be over'.

2⃣Second point goes into specifics. Due to their success, hundreds of dog coins are launched every day, but there are only a few repeatable successes that only few coins get right, one is a simple yet often overlooked fact. How do you make a dog coin special? Well you connect it to an actual existing dog, preferably of a celebrity. That's exactly what $MANEKI (Kenjiro Takada's dog), $NEIRO (Sanae Iwasaki's dog), $POPCAT (based on the cat named Oatmeal) and $FLOKI (Elon's Dog) all have in common. And so that's that rare thing that $SCOOT gets right too. It's Alex Becker's dog, the famous 9 figure entrepreneur with 1 million followers on X. And it's the first of its kind so there is no competition.

Why is that important? It gives a form of trust. When you name a dog after one specific (especially famous) character, it instantly becomes easily meme-able, and is almost treated like an animal social media instagram/twitter/Tik-Tok page, which makes it reliable, familiar and gives a form of trust to buy and hold as well as association with the value of the coin with the actual dog as long as the project is done right. 

Even more importantly, it gives value. Alex Becker is a nine figure entrepreneur, so his dog is likely valued accordingly, naturally, because he loves his dog and treats his animal also like a multi millionaire. 'The owner is worth hundreds of millions, so must the coin representing that dog'. And that's what has driven the price of previous specific crypto projects named after specific famous dogs. Requirement is that the crypto project is not consisting of lazy devs, so I researched into that as well. And they are indeed doing things right. Now I know Alex Becker isn't the prime figure to make a meme off. But remember that the meme is his dog, not him, which is also why the other memes I mentioned worked out.

3⃣I can't share names, but research ended in clear proof of partnerships with CEX's such as MEXC, bitmart and bitget, ready to go (i). Coingecko listing (key milestone for recognition) (ii) and finally, according to their wallet transfers, they have connections to no one other than Kaizen (iii), who is a direct connection to Becker himself. Finally, the contract is rug proof according to three scans (iv).

4⃣Further things they do right is good artwork, a funny and short name, no-roadmap policy, experienced devs and mods, and, smart telegram users I see re-occur time and time again in good projects. So it's indeed hard to unsee how connected they are and how much the network is already established even way before launch. 

5⃣ And it shows, my most important metric: avg messages per hour in tg is reaching on par versus other successful projects I have seen days after launch. May not be your usual metric, but I find it more important than telegram members or twitter followers, because the latter could be botted more easily (by insiders or people who want to curse the channel or get it banned). Although I did check and their 1,700 twitter followers seem legit, which is on par with $TREMP and $BODEN at launch. But overall, messages per hour is better. At the same time it projects the hype directly and gives confidence to buyers for social reasons.

Rushed projects do not do well typically, and ones that have been in the works for a long time, are better connected naturally. And now they just launched, pretty much right when everything is continuing up, in great alignment with my own bull thesis of a breakout soon. So not only did they start preparing at the right time, the people behind this project also know how to be patient and time a launch. Long preparation = long time staying with the project.

Why not:

Ichimoku cloud is another great indicator.

Quick disclaimers first:

As all simple TA methods, it falls for the same fallacy: it is a lagging indicator, so it only works if you are already sure about the conditions (else it turns into a fake-out).

But say you know the conditions (like we researched), then it can be used to confirm and to buy the dip.

Confirm conditions with: is price above cloud?
Have the two MA lines flipped (short term MA above long term)?
Has the cloud flipped green?

Two out of three is enough.

Good areas to buy the dip are the MA's and/or the cloud.

Not perfect, but way better than buying randomly and gets plenty of entries in even the most aggressive uptrends.

How do you calculate the risk levels?

Isn't it amazing how the market always finds a way to make the large majority lose? $BTC probably does it the best.

For instance:

➡️When the market has been ranging forever, it breaks out.
➡️When the market has been trending for a long time, it will start to range.
➡️When no volatility is expected, volatility kicks in.
➡️When volatility is expected, it's probably going to form a tight range.
➡️When a large news events comes (such as elections), most people tend to not position because it's dangerous and 'a gamble', yet it probably serves one of the cleanest high volume trades in a short time both ways.
➡️When most are positioned into altcoins, $BTC dominance rises.
➡️When most are positioned into $BTC, $BTC dominance drops.
➡️When a large altcoin narrative played out, people catch on, most position for it to continue, yet then the narrative most likely rotates to something completely different, like fashion trends.

I can keep going, but categorizing every single one of these helps you determine ways to not get burnt in every single way firstly, and secondly, find a counternarrative supporting your trade idea.

So it's not just 'up or down', there are many ways and reasons to both position or stay away from a market.

All disclaimers aside, let's get to it with the claim:

Claim

As the title saids: we won't see sub 50k anymore this year, 2024.

Analysis

So if you remember, I posted an educational post on OHLC theory (see quoted tweet), where, if the previous candles' high is taken, the previous candles low is likely not to be taken, during the same candle. In other words, a candle (including wicks) to fully engulf the previous candle is very unlikely. How (un)likely depends on the timeframe.

On the quarterly timeframe, a full engulfement happened to have occurred only once (on July 2015), throughout the entire lifetime of $BTC's history which is 60 quarterly candles long today.

So, because this quarterly candle has taken the previous quarter high, the chance that it takes previous quarter low (50k) by the end of this quarter, which aligns with the end of 2024, is only 1 in 60 or 1.67%.

So that means 50k won't be visited with a chance of 100% - 1.67% = 98.33%.

That's indeed direct proof that any bearishness towards sub 50k, just because we had a small move down, is likely exaggerated and emotionally based.

Conclusion

So this statement once again solidifies my statement of why this recent move up off the lows was so important and why we perform 4 data analyses, alongside heavy long-side positioning with it. And so far we're 27% in the green on $BTC.

This data also is a clear and non dubious way to showcase why and how the trending nature of $BTC works, confirming bullish data with more bullish data.

How do I start trading/investing if I only have $1000? A full guide

So, we're running both a 10k -> 100k trading challenge and a 200k -> 1 mil "investing" challenge all publicly on twitter and they are going well so far and we're making money.

But one question or comment I do often get asked is "well that's cool but what if I don't have 10k, or 200k, Astro?". Or more general: "How much do I need to get started with investing?". Or just people getting discouraged with: "well good for you that you're winning on all those positions, but I don't have that type of money and am not making nearly as much let alone making a living".

Firstly just wanted to address here to not let that demotivate you. But because the answer to those questions is slightly more nuanced, I'll get into those grey areas right here with this post because it would be unfair to just say "just start investing now and you will make it in 10 years".

Because it does depend to some extent to your strategy, incomes, capital available, where you come from. But regardless, it's a skill worth learning and if you want to make it, a skill you'll have to face mastering regardless of how much money you have, so why not start now? If you get good, things move quick. I'll show you how.

Skill is more important than capital

So, you all probably understand that trade-vesting is scalable, just like any business. I use trade-vesting here, a term for trading + investing that exist because doing both properly is essentially the same, investing is trading on a monthly/quarterly timeframe and yes most investors do sell assets too, ignore Michael Saylor here for a second.

Scalable means that your wealth general growths (or decreases if you're still learning) exponentially. I've shown that on the screenshot below.

And that's powerful, but also deceitful at the same time. It's powerful because regardless how much you have, 10x'ing is always practically the same, but the opposite (0.1x'ing) is also easy if you're not careful. That's why trading and investing is crucial to master, because if you don't and you have a lot of money from your day job, it's very easy to turn it into little money instead of more. So through scaling, climbing the ladder is much easier, as well as descending.

That's why getting through "the learners phase" (which we all have to) is critical to start doing as early as possible and also for as little cost/mistakes as possible. It would be disingenuous to tell you I didn't have my fair share of losses during my learners phase. It's not a joke when someone (me) tells you to "focus on the skill of making money over the money itself".

So with that said, don't worry for example if you turn 5k into 500 if that teaches you a valuable lesson. Those lessons are extremely valuable and don't even require any bit of journaling. "Your losses are your best journal".

What if you mastered the skill?

So that's the first point answered. It doesn't matter how much you have if you're in the learners phase. You just want to put your blood on the line, try to turn it into more, and stimulate the positive feedback loop and make money if you succeed. And stimulate the negative feedback loop and lose money when you lose. 

Okay but what if you're a skilled trade-vestor? What if you're past the learners phase? Well now the power of exponential returns is on your side. So let's say you 10x every 3 years after tax (I think that's very realistic), then whether you start with 1k or 10k to end up with ten million is just 12 or 15 years away, which is only a difference of three years. And that's why, yet again, it doesn't matter what you have, because trade-vesting is scalable.

And that shows why, as long as you have the skill of this craft, you're golden regardless, even if you have "nothing" and even if you lose everything sometime down the line, even twice (I know a couple).

What if I am broke?

Now I can hear you, "what if I literally have 1$, I want to turn it into 10 mil, that still takes me 21 years (assuming the same rate of 10x every 3 years).

Yes, I hear you. "Don't neglect your 9-to-5" is my answer. Because like I said, there is indeed nuance to this answer. And that's why I drew the graph below.

In short, the graph tells you that if you have a 9-5, it makes more sense to work for one hour instead of 3 years to turn your first dollar into 10$, and with dedication, it's very doable to save 10k or even more in a year or two. But the more you have, the less it makes sense to have a 9-to-5 until it makes 0 sense.

9-to-5 versus trade-vesting

I drew out a typical curve of what saving from a 9-to-5 could look like, versus the curve of a trade-vestor. Keep in mind that this chart is a logarithmic scale, so the 9-to-5'ers savings over time flatten out. The trade-vestor's curve should be linear. But because at the beginning, you're learning and focused on improving skill and mind (mindset/mentality), it starts slow and ultimately steepens. And once you're a master investor, it goes typically linear. 

Now you also see I drew it as flattening out afterwards. That's just for correctness, because as capital scales, liquidity becomes an issue. And to remain optimal your strategies require some change because multiplying millions of dollars isn't the same as thousands. So even returns of trade-vesting flatten out on the log scale. But don't worry, once that happens, you already made it by a long shot.

And I do understand it's a different story in a second or third world country in terms of saving money, but the principles still apply, the optimum to transition from more 9-to-5 towards trade-vesting just has to start with less capital, but the threshold of having made it in your country is lower at the same time. So everyone dedicated enough, can win up to the point of "making it" with a more or less even playing field regardless of your background. Explains why you see stories of people from a poor background make it.

Conclusion

Hope this posts gives some insight of "how much you need to invest". Not that much, really, perhaps a few months/a year of saving and time goes fast. But the most important point here is to start learning (or improving) it today because that will stick for a lifetime and the sooner you master it, the sooner exponential returns take over and can quit your 9-to-5, because the skill is a requirement.

"Focus on the skill of making money rather than making money itself", is not a joke or a meme, whenever someone (me) mentions that.

With that said I hope you are encouraged to keep learning and applying, to climb up that ladder and not slide down instead.

Regarding Stoplosses + guide on trading "without a stoploss"

So 5 days ago, we started a 10k -> 100k altcoin trading challenge where we show every single move for free on twitter for the world to copy.

It's been received very well (we're up 10% already despite missing some large moves by a hair) and the ones who followed have been making lots of money and at the same time actionably identifying ahead of everyone else and understanding how to trade these types of conditions. Teaching you how not to FOMO, but also not to miss out on essential moves by picking the right levels, timing and pair it with deep research of how I expect these conditions to evolve.

Easily the single most asked question is "why are you not using a stoploss".

It's a very common one because the standard of retail trading is to put a hard SL at a certain level, which the market makers can spot and run before they hit your profit levels.

Just kidding of course. But at least, "putting a hard SL is a must" is what the majority of trading gurus teach you because they all learnt trading from each other or like to echo chamber or just haven't considered an open mind to different options in an out of the box way. I'm not saying that is wrong. I use them myself.

But I come from quite a different background and besides that classical style of trading mentioned above, I also have some years in institutional trading which is indeed, mostly without a "stoploss".

See large hedge funds for instance don't have the ability to just close a position at a precise level at market (which is what a hard SL is). That would cause immense slippage. Instead they get out manually, upon invalidation of a certain market move on higher timeframes, which is also what we do. So, we still use an SL on this challenge, just not a hard SL.

"Okay so you use a manual SL, cool Astro, I get it but what if the market drops 80% overnight in a single H12 candle and we were long."

First of all, that's very unlikely to happen and only happened a few times in history across all crypto markets in the top 100. Only rug pulls have shown this behavior in the past.

Secondly, we don't go all in on one project (for the small chances it rug pulls or something), we'd still be fine even if that happens.

Thirdly, the only reason to use an SL is to take you out of the market in case it drops overnight and you are asleep. Otherwise, you can set alerts, see them as you're awake and get out manually. And because H12 candles are never bigger than 20% moves from open to close (back test this), and also because our leverage is never larger than 3x total, the chances of liquidation overnight are smaller than getting struck by lightning, which would kill you anyway.

And lastly, this is after all a limits only challenge, so setting an SL by default is an at market order. Reason for the limits only choice is because that is by far the easiest way to follow without missing out because you were not online. It also prevents large pools of liquidity (the SL I show) for the market makers to grab.

So with all of that, I hope you now both understand that trading without an SL is as low of a risk if not lower than exposing yourself to the market makers with a big flag showing where your forced losses are, as long as you know what you are doing, keep leverage low, and position accordingly. 

So instead of showing the market makers where they make us lose, I'm showcasing you the proper way of what it's like to be the market maker ourselves.

If you are still scared for a rug pull/overnight liquidation (this is crypto after all), I recommend putting a hard SL 30% down from original entry yourself, just to prevent that loss. Since our positions are smaller than half of size of the full account, that would only result in a 15% loss in the worst case of that low chance happening, as our picks are all focused on top 300 altcoins.

So accounting for all of that, I think this challenge is a nice refreshing change, to show you what's possible and that not every trade requires a hard SL, manual trading is possible even if you sleep 8 hours a day, and, it's working, isn't it?

Why I love market cycle theory - Part 2

So about 2 months ago, I've written an extensive part 1 on why I believe market cycles work so well, how to identify them and last but not least, not underestimate their power and effect especially in crypto but pretty much in every single market.

And the 15th of September wasn't a randomly picked time to make that post. It was just days after $BTC planted the major higher low at 53k in our opinion at the time, a low where we said, with at the time high conviction "this is very likely the last time $BTC visits low 50's, next time we go up and break out".

And here we are, nearly double prices today, at the time, I would say, something the world would not have ever believed so soon.

There was fear of recession, Warren buffet selling, OI at ATH's, Michael Bury going massively short, and the fud cutting rates (which typically means downside).

That's why I said, "market cycles are overarching and in control of markets and all of the above (such as monetary policy), so both respect cyclical theory and cyclical theory is leading both price and the factors mentioned above".

And I just wanted to mention another mechanism of why the 4 year cycle particularly works so well and it's quite simple:

For some reason, 4 years is the time it takes for people to completely forget what the same exact conditions were like exactly 4 years ago. Whether that was:

"What it felt like $BTC planting a bottom at 3k, and 4 years later at 15k". 
"What it felt like $BTC.D surging hard and $BTC pumping yet alts not doing anything"
"What it felt like for $ETH to not do anything and being called dead"
"And what it will feel like to 

It feels like 4 years is a good time to get fully attached to a narrative and expecting that to never change ever again. And if you have any friend groups in crypto (or just spend time on social media), you can see it. It's crystal clear and obvious.

"Memes have taken over"
"$BTC season will never end this time"
"$BTC will never stop ranging"
"This time is different than 4 years ago, whatever it may be"

Believe it or not but there also was a time (called Q1, Q2 2021) where alts were believed to be the new thing and $BTC was never going to take over a 50% market share ever again, never going back above 50% dominance because "the world adopted crypto and there are so many useful altcoins". And now, all those exact same altcoins are now called useless, meme, "speculation". Fascinating, isn't it. Those who were around, will understand what I mean.

So those phrases above are the ones that go around in the heads of the unaware people who don't track cycles to form some basic expectation and changes in narrative, because those narratives IMO do shift according to the overarching cycle, in crypto very prominent.

So not only by the very nature of 4 year cycles, but also the fact that 4 years seems to be the exact time when the majority forgets that narratives can change, that narrative indeed exactly shifts.

And that's important. You want the tides of the cycles on your side for the majority of your trades, or at least be aware of them. If you are, it becomes easy.

If you longed $BTC since Jan 2023, you never had more than a 40% drawdown, even if you were stupid enough to long the exact top. If you tried to short instead, you had to get out quick or try to anticipate ranges (be patient) or else get burnt hard.

If you shorted $BTC in 2022, you never had more than a 46% drawdown, even if you shorted exact bottoms.

If you bought alts during 2023-2024, you generally had a tough time and not much portfolio gain, many going to zero or slowly bleeding to zero, whilst $BTC maxis had and easy (and safe) ride.

I can keep going.

Of course, it's not always perfectly 3-1 year up-down pairs. There exist 2-2 year pairs or even 1-3 year pairs within a cycle and everything in between. But that's why you use other techniques to confirm what it will be because the market will through curveballs.

But typically, the cycle itself is 4 years, and that's a given, for the reasons mentioned.

And I think it will remain so for the rest of our lives.

We'll see. Always an open eye, but at the same time a critical eye to fundamental changes, not buying the idea that local narratives continue forever. And never will.

Good times don't last, bad times don't last.

Change is the only constant, but there are only limited classifications of situations, so that's why change is cyclical and why history rhymes.

As always, just my opinion, no need to agree anywhere.

Use a logic that works for you.
